rule: Per-player 500-tick timer (about 300 s) draws a random event only in the skilling afk state, one at a time, outside excluded zones. A visitor spawns next to the player with a 1000-tick lifetime (donor-marked guess), is tethered (row or more than 15 tiles brings it back), and escalates through four beats (wave, think, angry, fail); fail teleports the player; a talk releases the lock and pays out. Desert heat is a 150-tick countdown re-armed each cycle, shortened by armour and lengthened by desert clothing; each cycle either drinks one water step or takes 1-10 damage with no water. Animals idle on timers (sheep 20-39, duck 50-99, cow 15-34 ticks). Defect D1: the lost path releases no lock, so no further random events until login (macro_events.rs2:67, :152; old man :17-21, :46-50, :73).
keep: One random event at a time per player (lock)
Area exclusions as zone data (duel arena, tutorial, minigame zones)
Visitor needs one reply, or leaves after four beats
Tether: visitor brought back when out of row or beyond range
Small hidden countdown that gear modifies (fits gear dressing as data)
Idle animal timers with a species-specific gap range
Measured idle gap recorded in the source (duck averages) as a design note
change: Release the lock on every exit path, including the lost path (D1; sketch endVisitor)
Measure the 1000-tick lifetime on a phone instead of trusting the donor guess (D2)
Decide whether a fail should teleport or just leave (D3, Dom call)
Write our own speech lines, names, desert and visitor looks
look_test: Target origins/server/world-spawns.ts (row 23). Look-test flag on one scene: a visitor beside the player with one speech line and one emote per beat, a puff on leave; run the four beats at donor pace and faster, then the fail teleport; compare with a plain scene; Dom judges whether he can read the beat without looking away, whether the fail feels fair, and whether the idle sounds at 20 s and 60 s gaps make the field feel alive.
